summary:
The main idea behind our Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is different from a typical game. Most games show a Game Over screen when a player makes a mistake. Our project takes a different approach: it shows how each decision can affect the rest of the mission and its future outcome.
For example, if an astronaut ignores oxygen levels, skips safety checks, or makes a poor decision while exploring, the consequences can affect the mission later. Instead of simply punishing the player, the simulator helps them understand why their decisions matter.
We want students to experience the challenges of lunar exploration, learn from their mistakes, and see how careful planning and decision-making can make a mission successful. Our goal is not just to make another space game, but to create an interactive learning experience where every action has a consequence and every mistake becomes a lesson.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Our project, Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, is a 3D space exploration simulator that allows users to experience different activities performed by astronauts during a Moon mission.

The main idea behind this project is to make learning about space exploration more interesting and interactive. Instead of just reading about astronauts and their missions, users can experience the activities through a virtual environment.

The mission starts with the astronaut entering a lunar habitat, preparing the spacesuit, checking oxygen and pressure systems, and completing the required safety procedures. After completing the preparation, the astronaut can explore the lunar surface, operate a lunar rover, discover geological sample locations, inspect lunar rocks and collect samples.

The project provides an engaging way to understand how astronauts prepare for space missions and perform scientific activities on the Moon.

Benefits and Impact

This project helps students develop an interest in space science and understand the challenges involved in lunar exploration. It provides a practical learning experience without requiring expensive physical equipment. It also encourages curiosity, problem-solving and learning through exploration.

Our aim is to make space education more accessible and interesting, especially for students who are curious about astronomy, engineering and space technology.

Technologies Used

We developed this project using React.js, TypeScript and Vite for the frontend. Three.js, React Three Fiber and Drei are used to create the 3D environment and interactive objects. We used CSS for styling, Google Antigravity IDE for development, Puppeteer for testing, and Git and GitHub for version control.

We also used AI-assisted development tools to help with coding, debugging and improving the application.

Creativity and Innovation

The unique part of our project is that it combines education with an interactive gaming experience. Users are not just watching a space simulation; they can actually control an astronaut, perform mission activities, drive a lunar rover and collect geological samples.

We have included features such as interactive habitat equipment, spacesuit preparation, lunar terrain, rover driving, geological scanning and mission progress tracking.

This makes the project different from a normal educational website because users learn by performing activities themselves.

Factors Considered During Development

While developing the project, we focused on making the simulation realistic, easy to use and engaging. We considered the appearance of the lunar environment, astronaut movement, rover controls, mission instructions and overall performance.

We also focused on keeping the project expandable so that more missions, vehicles, environments and activities can be added in the future.

Overall, our goal is to create an educational space exploration experience where students can learn about astronaut activities in an interactive and enjoyable way.
